# dotcommoners

> Open-source organization building high-performance, self-hostable infrastructure and systems software. Written primarily in Rust, Zig, and Python for self-hosters and platform engineers. Everything is open source (MIT) and designed to run on your own hardware with no vendor lock-in.

dotcommoners rebuilds the infrastructure most teams rent — orchestration, streaming, browser automation, observability — as open source you own and operate yourself.

## Site pages

- [Home](https://www.dotcommoners.com/): What dotcommoners is, the "own don't rent your infrastructure" thesis, project portfolio, and who it's for.
- [Projects](https://www.dotcommoners.com/projects): Full descriptions of every public open-source project with links to repos and docs, plus the domain taxonomy (orchestration, streaming, browser automation, observability).
- [Principles](https://www.dotcommoners.com/principles): The six principles behind every project — open source (MIT), self-hostable by default, performance-first, brokerless, no vendor lock-in, readable and documented.
- [About & Manifesto](https://www.dotcommoners.com/about): The open-source, self-hostable, no-lock-in philosophy; who's behind it; how to contribute.
- [FAQ](https://www.dotcommoners.com/faq): High-intent answers — is it MIT, can I self-host, what languages, how to contribute, vs SaaS.
- [Contact](https://www.dotcommoners.com/contact): Get in touch with the team.

## Deep dives

Long-form write-ups on the architecture, operations, licensing and problem domains behind the projects. Each names the cases where the approach is the wrong one.

- [Brokerless architecture](https://www.dotcommoners.com/brokerless): What a central message broker actually does, where it becomes the ceiling, how a peer-to-peer NNG mesh agrees on state with bloom filters, merkle trees and vector clocks, and when keeping the broker is the better decision.
- [Rust, Zig and Python](https://www.dotcommoners.com/languages): Why the data plane and the control plane want different languages; garbage collection, per-connection memory, static binaries, and the honest note that no public dotcommoners project is written in Rust yet.
- [Self-hosting: what you take on](https://www.dotcommoners.com/self-hosting): The operational contract — hosts, kernels, upgrades, capacity measurement, secrets, runbooks — plus each project's real host requirements and a readiness checklist.
- [Self-hosted vs managed SaaS](https://www.dotcommoners.com/vs-saas): Cost shape, operational burden, data path, upgrade timing and exit cost, including the cases where a managed service is the better engineering decision.
- [MIT licensing](https://www.dotcommoners.com/licensing): What the MIT grant permits, how it compares with BSD, Apache-2.0, LGPL, GPL, AGPL and source-available licences, and what it deliberately withholds (warranty, support, express patent grant, trademark).
- [Browser automation at fleet scale](https://www.dotcommoners.com/browser-automation): Placement, isolation, idle cost and recovery — the four problems that appear when one headless browser becomes a thousand.
- [Real-time streaming at scale](https://www.dotcommoners.com/real-time-streaming): Why millions of long-lived SSE connections is a memory and fan-out problem, transport comparison, topic routing, and authentication under reconnect storms.
- [Observability you own](https://www.dotcommoners.com/observability): Cardinality, retention, resolution, egress and sampling as cost drivers. Problem-domain only — dotcommoners has no observability project published yet.

## Public projects

Each project has its own site on a dotcommoners subdomain.

- [Machineuse](https://machineuse.dotcommoners.com/) — site: https://machineuse.dotcommoners.com/ · repo: https://github.com/dotcommoners/machineuse · Distributed container management for browser automation at scale. Create, schedule, and manage isolated browser instances across many worker nodes with intelligent scheduling, brokerless NNG messaging, and snapshot-based dormancy. Language: Python. Docs: https://docs.dotcommoners.com/machineuse/
- [RevenProx](https://revenprox.dotcommoners.com/) — site: https://revenprox.dotcommoners.com/ · repo: https://github.com/dotcommoners/revenprox · A high-performance, horizontally scalable Server-Sent Events (SSE) proxy built in Zig for real-time event streaming at scale. Designed for 10M+ concurrent connections across 100+ instances using a brokerless NNG mesh, with JWT authentication and topic-based routing. Language: Zig. Docs: https://docs.dotcommoners.com/revenprox/

## Family of sites

- https://www.dotcommoners.com — the organization site (this site): thesis, projects, principles, deep dives.
- https://machineuse.dotcommoners.com — Machineuse: distributed browser automation. Features, architecture, use cases, comparison, quickstart, FAQ.
- https://revenprox.dotcommoners.com — RevenProx: Zig SSE proxy. Features, architecture, use cases, comparison, quickstart, FAQ.
- https://docs.dotcommoners.com — reference documentation for both projects.

## Key facts

- Organization: dotcommoners (https://github.com/dotcommoners)
- License: MIT (permissive, open source)
- Deployment model: self-hosted / on-premise, no SaaS lock-in
- Primary languages: Rust, Zig, Python
- Documentation: https://docs.dotcommoners.com
- Contact: contact@dotcommoners.com
